name: Rijksmuseum
notes: Pierre Cuypers's Rijksmuseum (1885; renovated by Cruz y Ortiz, 2013): red brick with stone bands, about 140 by 90 m, set at its true angle on the Singelgracht (from the OpenStreetMap ground); four wings round two courts now roofed in glass as atria, the public passage cut through the middle at ground level, steep slate roofs, the lantern over the middle, the twin towers and gable of the entrance front on the Stadhouderskade and corner pavilions; the Museumplein and its long pool behind. From general knowledge of the building; no photographs were available. Tower and roof heights, the window rhythm and the corner pavilions are approximate. Refined 30 Sep 2026 (no photographs reachable; the ground file's OpenStreetMap outlines and published descriptions): the whole place moved 12 m west and 12 m south onto the building's outline; the Philips Wing added at the south-west corner, where the ground has a separate block of about five storeys (brick with a stone band, flat slate top — its form guessed); the great roofs made blue-grey slate rather than black, so the brick below and the glass over the atria read against them.
